comment: The revert-checks of the question predicate (issue #243): every reader takes the escalation's `**The decision:**` line, and only a comment without that marker falls back to its first non-empty line. The escalation comment opens with its verdict word, so the fallback alone answers `needs-decision` and an answer binds to `<!-- answers: needs-decision -->` — measured on #196's own answer. One mutation per implementation, because the shell readers share one jq program and the Java core restates it: A1.1 mutates the program in `tools/issues/lib.sh` (read by `decisions.sh` and `answer.sh`), A1.2 the restatement in `WorkPackage.java`. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/decision-question-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how and `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule.

mutations.label: A1.1
mutations.why: the marker line being the question — without it the first non-empty line is the escalation's verdict word

mutations.label: A1.2
mutations.why: the same rule in the work package's fallback, which the answer's marker now makes rare but not absent
